rows.parameter: Effective pupil diameter across a track
rows.value: 8.5 m down to 5.5 m
rows.quote: equivalent to a change in the effective pupil diameter from ... 8.5 m to 5.5 m
rows.note: HANDLING: the illuminated pupil changes with the track (area, centroid and shape), so the collecting area is not fixed. The preset keeps D = 10 m (the pupil diameter); R does not depend on it (R depends on the 93 um slit, the f/8 collimator and the echelle). D enters only the arcsec bookkeeping and any collecting-area estimate. Because the explorer's F is the collimator's f/8 (virtual convention), its focal length (80 m) is not the HET's 36.5 m: the on-sky plate scale of 5.65 arcsec/mm is in the note, not in the state. A throughput or S/N estimate with D = 10 m overstates the collecting area by (10/7)^2 = 2.0 against the 7 m the design papers assume. The preset note must say this.

rows.parameter: Input (re-imaging) optics between the fiber puck and the collimator
rows.value: CaF2 and SFTM-16 lenses: f/3.3 fiber output re-imaged to f/8; magnification 8 / 3.3 = 2.42
rows.quote: Input optics made from CaF2 and SFTM-16 reimage the input fiber feed from f/3.3 (accounting for FRD from the telescope input of f/3.65) to the f/8 that the off-axis parabola is expecting
rows.note: DERIVED: 8 / 3.3 = 2.424. The f/3.3 is the fiber's output ratio after focal ratio degradation of the f/3.65 input (a faster beam). WHERE THE SLIT SITS: the nickel slit is glued on the puck that terminates the three fibers (K18 Sec. 2, Fig. 14 caption: 'The fused silica puck is used to terminate the three fibers'), so it stands in the f/3.3 space and the input optics image it, with the fiber faces, onto the collimator's focal plane at f/8 (INFERRED: no source draws the order of puck, slit and input optics, but the slit is on the puck and the puck is the fiber end). In the collimator's focal plane the 93 um slit is 93 x 2.424 = 225.5 um wide and the 312 um core 756.4 um across.

rows.parameter: Collimator input focal ratio F_out (explorer's virtual convention)
rows.quote: to the f/8 that the off-axis parabola is expecting
rows.note: The explorer is entered with F = 8 and D = 10 m (virtual convention of web/presets.js: slit = slit width in the collimator's focal plane / (F_out x D); fcol = F x W = 1600 mm). The explorer's F is therefore NOT the HET's f/3.65 and its focal length (80 m) is not the HET's 36.5 m. On-sky equivalents (DERIVED): the 93 um slit in the f/3.3 fiber space is 93 / 312 = 0.298 of the 312 um core (1.77 arcsec at 5.65 arcsec/mm), i.e. 0.52 arcsec at the focus with f/3.65 input (0.5256 = 93 um x 5.65 arcsec/mm); the explorer's 0.5813 arcsec is that angle times 3.65 / 3.3 = 1.106, the FRD speed-up of the fiber beam.

rows.parameter: Slit width entered in the explorer (virtual arcsec at D = 10 m, F = 8)
rows.quote: reimage the input fiber feed from f/3.3
rows.note: DERIVED: (93 um x 8 / 3.3 = 225.45 um at the collimator's focal plane) / (8 x 10 000 mm) x 206 264.8 = 0.5813 arcsec. Equivalent: slit angle at the collimator = 225.45 um / 1600 mm = 1.409e-4 rad. The slit, not the fiber core, sets the line width, so the fiber is entered as a slit (no sqrt3/2 factor).

rows.note: M14 settles the cross-disperser: a VPH (the 2010 and 2012 papers described a 150 l/mm and a 110 g/mm grism). No prism or glass dispersion formula is needed and no cryogenic indices enter: the model's VPH is a transmission grating at its Bragg setting. 'Higher groove density on the VPH' follows from the asymmetric pupil (a smaller beam at the VPH); its value is NOT FOUND.

Fit with physics.js (scratch scan2.js) for the state of this record (f_col 1600, f_cam 362, 74.6 deg): VPH 210 /mm at lambda_c 10500 A puts 28 orders, m = 75 to 48, on the chip with 8077-12792 A, against the published 8080-12780 A and 28 orders (and Fig. 1 of M14 labels orders 48 to 74 with the next order cut by the chip edge). Neighbors: 200/10500 gives 31 orders (7960-13019 A), 220/10500 gives 27 (8188-12778 A), 210/10400 gives 29 (7979-12786 A). Not independent of the coverage it reproduces.

rows.note: The focal length is NOT FOUND (M14: 'Details of the spectrograph optical design merits its own paper'). EFFECTIVE: fitted to Ninan 2019's 9.5 px slit length: the 312 um core is magnified 8 / 3.3 by the input optics to 756.4 um at the collimator, so 9.5 px x 18 um = 171.0 um needs f_cam / f_col = 171.0 / 756.4 = 0.2261, f_cam = 0.2261 x 1600 = 362 mm. The same ratio makes the 93 um slit 225.45 x 0.2261 = 51.0 um = 2.83 px wide (geometric); the model's FWHM is 2.71 px against N19's 2.5 px (8% high). The 2012 'f/2' would make the camera beam 181 mm (INFERRED, the asymmetric pupil's demagnification 181/200 = 0.905). The 2012 and 2010 values (f/2, f/2.3; 400 mm) are superseded.

Camera focal length (EFFECTIVE 362 mm, fitted to N19's 9.5 px slit length), the beam diameter as such (M14 gives only the 200 mm x 800 mm grating; 200 mm is M12's beam), the off-axis distance or tilt of the collimator, the pupil-transfer focal length of the asymmetric white pupil, and every layout distance except the 8 ft bench (M14 Figs. 2-3 are exterior views of the cryostat and radiation shield with no optics).
VPH cross-disperser groove density, Bragg angle and the camera-collimator angle (M14 and the 2019 talk say only 'VPH', 'higher groove density'). The explorer value (210 /mm) is EFFECTIVE.
As-built out-of-plane angle gamma (M12: 0.5 deg design; K18's 4.4 deg slit rotation suggests a larger one).

Spacing of the science, sky and calibration traces across the dispersion (N19 Fig. 2 and M14 Fig. 1 show them without a scale); the order of puck, slit and input optics along the fiber path is not drawn (the slit is on the puck: K18).
A measured resolving power from arc, etalon or comb lines (every source quotes R ~ 50,000, 53,000 or 55,000 without a method); measured dispersion in A/px; end-to-end throughput.
The mosaic layout of the echelle as built (two 200 x 400 mm segments is INFERRED from the 2012 Fig. 6).
conflicts: Echelle blaze: 74.6 deg as manufactured (M14) against R4 = 75.96 deg (K18's 'R4 echelle') and '75 degrees' (M10, M12). 74.6 deg adopted: it reproduces the published order edges (ME19) to 0.07%, against 0.6-0.7% for 75.96 deg.

Collimator and input optics: the 2012 paper's f/3.65 fiber feed and 200 mm beam suggested a 730 mm collimator (the earlier version of this record); M14 says the input optics re-image f/3.3 to f/8, so the collimator is f/8 (1600 mm for 200 mm). 2012: 'a 200 mm beam'; 2010: 150 mm (M10); M12 Fig. 6 caption: 150-200 mm.
Cross-disperser: 150 l/mm grism (M10, 2010), 110 g/mm grism (M12, 2012), VPH (M14 2014, NS 2019). M14 wins.
Camera: f/2.3 (M10), f/2 (M12), 'fast' with no number (M14). EFFECTIVE 362 mm adopted (2012's f/2 with a 200 mm beam gave 400 mm; the 9.5 px slit image of N19 with the f/8 collimator needs 362 mm).
White pupil: symmetric single large mirror in the 2012 Fig. 6; 'asymmetric white pupil ... the design adopted for HPF' (M14, NS).
Resolving power: 50,000 (design: M14, M12, S16), 55,000 (talk NS, KA20 and most science papers), 53,000 (ME19). The explorer's geometric R (51,300) lies within 7% of all three.
Operating temperature: 200 K design (M12 Sec. 3.4) against 180 K built (M14, S16, K18).
